analysis: Both units are CHANGELOG.md text only (head lines ~416-617+). No executable code, config, or workflow changes were supplied, so no concrete security regression can be shown from these units. The entries match the base threat model: the v0.9.9 and v0.9.8 entries describe the 30-minute-TTL-era SSD cache, half-of-available-disk budget and 20 GiB reserve (T-041), and the private-only roster exclusion, durable build qualification, per-dispatch revocation fencing and the opt-in MDM-optional App Attest path (TB-011, T-052..T-058). The newest 'App Attest failure diagnostics' entry describes provider `ready` replies with diagnostics outside the signed transcript (launch session, boot time, SIP/SSV status, key history, APNs push receipt history, native error codes), which the coordinator drops if invalid and which do not affect authorization. That is consistent with the TB-002 diagnostic-boundary paragraph, which is labelled as covering diagnostic metadata only. Source for that behavior was not supplied. Other claims are likewise unverified here: the new `/app-attest/diagnostics` admin endpoint (TB-006 admin boundary, A-015/T-058 identifier exposure), `darkbloom report` under sudo reading the invoking user's credentials and state, the APNs push outcome metrics (the changelog says no identifiers in tags), and derivation of reboot/restart from provider timestamps. A reviewer of the corresponding code should confirm that diagnostics are bounded and never feed authorization (T-052, T-053), that the admin endpoint is authenticated and does not leak stable identifiers (T-058), and that the sudo credential-reading path does not migrate or expose tokens. A small residual: T-041 states releases through v0.9.10 deleted retired kv files, while this changelog's latest section is v0.9.9 and a 15-to-30 minute TTL change is not visible here. That is documentation consistency only, not a finding.
